verdicts.title: IdentityStrategy.sensitivity ignores the participation schema, so bare mf_gaussian under-reports epsilon by sqrt(k)
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end on the current tree. packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_identity.py:45-46 is still `def sensitivity(self, **_) -> float: return 1.0`, and _mf_gaussian.py:132-141 feeds exactly that value to _native.mf_gaussian_pld as the sensitivity of the whole bare release. Measured with `uv run python`: identity_strategy().sensitivity(n_steps=1000, min_sep=100, max_participations=5) = 1.0 (identical to the k=1 value), while every sibling scales: band_mf 1.00000->2.23607, bsr 1.16046->2.59486, lambda_cgd 1.00000->2.23607, bisr 1.00000->2.69449, blt 1.80457->4.64553. fa.mf_gaussian(1.0, identity_strategy(), n_steps=1000, min_sep=100, max_participations=5).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 4.37717809602987; the correct value for a C=I release with 5 participations (sensitivity sqrt(5), equivalently 5-fold Gaussian self-composition) is da.gaussian(1/sqrt(5)).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 11.480022787731485. The math is unambiguous: for C=I the schema sensitivity max_pi ||sum_{j in pi} e_j|| = sqrt(k), which is also just Gaussian composition. I independently checked every escape hatch the audit note claims and they hold: the Poisson amplifier takes the IdentityStrategy branch and sets effective_nm = noise_multiplier directly with num_groups = n_steps self-composition (_poisson.py:188-190); b_min_sep asks explicitly for min_sep=n_steps, max_participations=1 (_b_min_sep/__init__.py:166-169), which is the correct kappa=1 for identity; _balls_in_bins.py never calls sensitivity; _second_moment.py:140-145 also asks for k=1. So the defect is confined to the bare (unamplified) MfGaussian.pld path with IdentityStrategy, and no amplified path is affected. No test pins the buggy value: packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/accounting/test_identity_mf.py only exercises n_steps=1 plus explicit self-composition (lines 44-71). Mitigation, not refutation: docs/reference/accounting.md:420 and docs/user-guide/accounting.md:280 do warn 'Do not use bare calls with these strategies to budget repeated participation'. But the API fails open - it accepts min_sep/max_participations, ignores them, and returns a number - and the surrounding guidance in the same doc section ('For bare accounting, declare the full horizon') invites exactly the call that goes wrong. Not critical: the sanctioned DP-SGD-via-MF paths (n_steps=1 then *T, or a poisson/b_min_sep/balls_in_bins wrapper) are correct. ALREADY TRACKED: open issue #359 ('Define BandMF participation sensitivity and price second moments consistently', state=open, labels bug/blocked/needs-design/severity: high/impact: epsilon) has as its first acceptance criterion 'Charged privacy cost is non-decreasing in max_participations for every strategy' and as its proposed direction 'Define whether strategy sensitivity is single-participation or participation-aware, then make all callers explicit'. e44d6ab6 (#998) satisfied that for BandMF only; IdentityStrategy is the residual of the same open issue, not a new defect.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Only the bare, unamplified MF accounting path is affected: `opaque.dpftrl.accounting.mf_gaussian(sigma, identity_strategy(), n_steps=N, ...)` with N > 1. IdentityStrategy.sensitivity accepts and discards min_sep/max_participations and always returns 1.0, so MfGaussian.pld prices the release as a single sensitivity-1 Gaussian regardless of the declared schema. Measured on 12146ec4: mf_gaussian(1.0, identity_strategy(), n_steps=1000, min_sep=100, max_participations=5).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 4.3772, while the correct value at sensitivity sqrt(5) is 11.4800 - a 2.62x silent under-report in the unsafe direction. The gap grows as sqrt(k); the default schema (min_sep=1, max_participations=None -> n_steps) declares k = n_steps, so the same call without explicit schema args returns the identical 4.3772 for what is really a sqrt(1000)-sensitivity release. No warning or exception is raised. All five sibling strategies (band_mf, blt, bsr, bisr, lambda_cgd) scale correctly at the same point; identity is the sole outlier. Amplified accounting (poisson, b_min_sep, balls_in_bins), the paired second-moment allocator, and the sanctioned n_steps=1 + self-compose pattern are all unaffected - each either bypasses identity sensitivity or explicitly requests the k=1 value. A documented caveat at docs/reference/accounting.md:420 and docs/user-guide/accounting.md:280 tells users not to make this call, but the API fails open rather than refusing.

verdicts.title: Reference and user-guide accounting docs still claim bare BandMF sensitivity accounts for one participation
verdicts.reasoning: Verified every link. The sentence 'Bare BandMF and Identity sensitivity currently accounts for one participation. Do not use bare calls with these strategies to budget repeated participation.' is present verbatim at docs/reference/accounting.md:420 and docs/user-guide/accounting.md:280 (grep found exactly these two occurrences). It is measurably false for BandMF on this tree: band_mf_strategy(bands=100).sensitivity(n_steps=1000, min_sep=100, max_participations=5) = 2.23607 vs 1.00000 at (min_sep=n_steps, max_participations=1) - I ran this. The code at _band_mf.py:138-187 computes k via minsep_true_max_participations and returns sqrt(minsep_sensitivity_upper_bound(...)) whenever k > 1, with the column norm only on the k == 1 shortcut. docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/band-mf.md:74-76 and :177-183 state the opposite and correct behaviour ('returns this value; pass min_sep=n_steps, max_participations=1 to ask for kappa instead' / 'Pass the participation schema you actually run under ... because the bare PLD is calibrated to the schema sensitivity S'). `git show --stat e44d6ab6` confirms the commit touched docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/band-mf.md but neither docs/reference/accounting.md nor docs/user-guide/accounting.md. The Identity half of the sentence remains true (finding 12). SEVERITY DOWNGRADED from medium to low: there is no epsilon impact and no wrong result. The stale half misdirects a reader away from functionality that now works, which is the conservative direction. The finding's secondary argument - that a reader who spots the BandMF error will discount the Identity warning and thereby lose the only published guard against the real under-report - is a plausible chain but entirely speculative; I could not establish it as anything beyond a hypothesis. Not a duplicate of any open issue: #359 is about code, and #775/#845 are a citation-verification umbrella; this staleness was created on 2026-09-11 by e44d6ab6, after those issues were written.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: docs/reference/accounting.md:420 and docs/user-guide/accounting.md:280 carry an identical sentence that is factually false for BandMF since e44d6ab6 (2026-09-11): BandMfStrategy.sensitivity has been schema-aware for two weeks (verified: 1.00000 at k=1 vs 2.23607 at min_sep=100, max_participations=5 for n_steps=1000), and docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/band-mf.md - changed by the same commit - documents the new behaviour twice. A user reading the reference or the user guide is told not to use bare BandMF multi-participation accounting, which now works correctly; that is a utility loss in the conservative direction, not a privacy loss. The Identity half of the same sentence is still accurate and is the only published warning about the IdentityStrategy defect, so the sentence must be split rather than deleted. Docs-only; no code path or epsilon value changes.

verdicts.title: 60 KB internal research/diary document issue-795-research.md committed at the repository root and never removed
verdicts.reasoning: Fully verified, including the packaging half the note flagged as 'most likely'. `ls -la issue-795-research.md` -> 60,100 bytes, 1064 lines, at the repository root alongside AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, README.md and SECURITY.md (the only other root *.md files). `git log --oneline --all -- issue-795-research.md` returns exactly one commit, d09d7b9a 'fix(dpftrl): bound BISR noise state by bandwidth (#886)' - nothing removes it. The content is a dated development diary: line 1 '# Issue 795: bounded-memory BISR noise execution', line 3 'Research snapshot: 2026-08-31 UTC', line 5 '## Post-research implementation update (2026-09-01 UTC)', then rebase SHAs, PR #857 narrative and internal GitHub links; grep finds 'follow-up work but is not a condition' at :31, 'possible follow-ups' at :125 and 'should be tracked as follow-up work' at :1012. That is precisely what the AGENTS.md Documentation section rules out ('Keep user-facing docs and code comments diary-free ... Migration narrative belongs in PR bodies and the changelog'). I settled the sdist question by building it: there is no MANIFEST.in, and `uv run --with build python -m build --sdist` produced opaque-0.15.6rc2.dev22+gbd83bbb0.tar.gz which contains opaque-0.15.6rc2.dev22+gbd83bbb0/issue-795-research.md - so the file does ship inside the root sdist, as setuptools_scm includes all git-tracked files by default. The wheel claim also holds: pyproject.toml:67-74 declares py-modules = [] and packages.find include = []/exclude = ['*']. Severity stays low: repo hygiene and a stale internal document in a published sdist, no functional or privacy impact.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A 1064-line, 60,100-byte working document named issue-795-research.md sits at the repository root, added by d09d7b9a and never removed. It is a dated research snapshot ('Research snapshot: 2026-08-31 UTC', 'Post-research implementation update (2026-09-01 UTC)') with rebase SHAs, PR-by-PR narrative and internal issue links, including statements about work as pending that has since merged. It sits next to README.md, SECURITY.md and LICENSE, where a browser of the repository root will take it for project documentation, and it violates the AGENTS.md diary-free rule. Confirmed by building the sdist: the file is included in the root `opaque` sdist (verified in opaque-0.15.6rc2.dev22+gbd83bbb0.tar.gz), since the root project has no MANIFEST.in and setuptools_scm ships git-tracked files. No wheel carries it (pyproject.toml:67-74 declares no packages). No functional or privacy impact.

verdicts.title: docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/bisr.md carries issue-tracker and roadmap narrative in a user-facing mechanism reference
verdicts.reasoning: Verified verbatim at docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/bisr.md:112-118: 'This bounded ring is the complete `O(p)` execution design required by [issue #795](https://github.com/JetBrains-Research/opaque/issues/795).' followed by 'PRNG replay could trade that persistent tensor storage for extra noise generation, but replay and a reusable generic banded-inverse executor are follow-up directions rather than requirements for this bounded BISR path.' `git log -- docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/bisr.md` confirms d09d7b9a is the most recent commit to the file. AGENTS.md Documentation section forbids both the development-history framing and forward references to features that do not exist. I additionally checked the referenced issue: #795 is CLOSED (state_reason completed, closed 2026-09-02 by PR #886), so the reference points a user at a closed internal tracker item - pure development history with no current meaning. The surrounding factual content the finding says should stay is indeed present and correct in the source: _bisr runtime state keeps min(p, n_steps) - 1 iid draws with O(min(p, n_steps) * model_size) storage, and the checkpoint-layout warning at :121-140 is a genuine user-facing caveat. I did not re-run the numerical BISR equivalence measurements quoted in the note's evidence (3 buffers at bandwidth=4, 3.7e-15 relative agreement) - those were not needed to establish the docs claim and I treat them as unverified context. Note the finding correctly does not flag the second tracker link at :136-138 (open issue #789 on calibrated DP-FTRL resume), which is a legitimate user-facing warning about an open bug. Severity low: documentation style/staleness, no functional, numerical or privacy impact.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/bisr.md:112-118, in a user-facing mechanism reference, tells the reader that the bounded ring is 'the complete O(p) execution design required by issue #795' - an issue that is now closed (completed 2026-09-02 via PR #886) - and adds a roadmap sentence describing PRNG replay and a generic banded-inverse executor as 'follow-up directions'. A user consulting the page to size BISR's memory cost is handed an internal tracker number and a forward reference that reads as a commitment, instead of a plain statement of the current cost. AGENTS.md forbids both. The factual half of the same section (the y_t formula, the min(p, n_steps) - 1 retained draws, the O(min(p, n_steps) * model_size) statement, and the checkpoint-layout warning) is accurate and should stay, as should the separate link at :136-138 to open issue #789. Documentation-only; no code, numerical or privacy impact.
